overview: Premature ventricular contractions are extra heartbeats originating from an ectopic focus within the ventricles. They occur earlier than expected and interrupt the normal cardiac rhythm. PVCs are common and often benign in individuals without structural heart disease, but frequent PVCs may be associated with cardiomyopathy, ventricular tachycardia, sudden cardiac death risk in susceptible patients, and worsening cardiac function.
ecg_clues: premature beat occurring earlier than expected
broad qrs complex greater than or equal to 120 ms
discordant st segment and t wave changes
absence of preceding normal sinus p wave
ecg_limitations: ecg alone cannot determine symptom severity
ecg alone cannot determine cardiomyopathy presence
ecg alone cannot determine underlying ischemic heart disease
single pvc may be benign and clinically insignificant
ecg alone cannot determine long term pvc burden without monitoring
complications: sudden cardiac death in susceptible patients

history_questions: Do symptoms occur after caffeine intake?
Do symptoms occur during stress or anxiety?
Have you had a previous heart attack?
Have you been diagnosed with heart failure?

when_to_seek_help: known heart disease with pvc symptoms

followup_questions.syncope: Have you fainted or nearly fainted recently?
followup_questions.chest_pain: Do you experience chest pain during episodes?
followup_questions.history_of_mi: Have you had a heart attack before?
followup_questions.coronary_artery_disease: Have you been diagnosed with coronary artery disease?
followup_questions.heart_failure: Have you been diagnosed with heart failure?
followup_questions.cardiomyopathy: Have you been diagnosed with cardiomyopathy?
followup_questions.caffeine_use: How much caffeine do you consume daily?
followup_questions.alcohol_use: How often do you drink alcohol?
followup_questions.smoking_status: Do you currently smoke or use tobacco products?

confidence_rules: wide premature qrs strongly increases confidence
multiple qrs morphologies suggest multifocal pvc
three or more consecutive pvc beats increase vt suspicion
agent_reasoning_hints: isolated pvc in healthy individuals is often benign
frequent pvc burden increases cardiomyopathy risk
multifocal pvc generally indicates greater electrical instability
couplets and nsvt increase ventricular arrhythmia concern
pvc occurring on prolonged qtc may trigger torsades de pointes
underlying coronary artery disease increases clinical significance
underlying heart failure increases clinical significance
source_notes: PVCs are considered frequent when more than 5 per minute on routine ECG
PVCs are considered frequent when more than 10 to 30 per hour on ambulatory monitoring
Bigeminy means every other beat is a PVC
Trigeminy means every third beat is a PVC
Quadrigeminy means every fourth beat is a PVC
Three to thirty consecutive PVCs may be classified as non sustained ventricular tachycardia
Frequent PVC burden may cause PVC induced cardiomyopathy
PVCs occurring during prolonged QT may trigger torsades de pointes
